title: Complete B18 in siyumim_timeline_and_lifetime_providers_test.dart to actually exercise the unmark-after-mark ledger conflict it documents

evidence.quote:
// Then unmark the same seder — FIRST-WRITE WINS per putIfAbsent,
// so the positive mark placed first takes priority.

why: B18's name and inline comments describe adding a positive seder mark then an unmark entry for the same seder, asserting the 'first (positive) mark' wins per putIfAbsent. The actual ledgerEntries list (lines 1143-1156) contains only the single positive entry -- the unmark _fakeLedgerData call described in the comment was never written -- so B18 exercises nothing beyond a trivial single-entry seder expansion already covered by B17, under a misleading name. computeLearnedLeafRefs' putIfAbsent (builder) plus getEntriesByCurriculum/getEntriesByTrack's orderBy(desc(completedAt)) (DAO) together implement a real 'most-recent-ledger-action-wins' contract with no shared documentation and no runtime assertion tying the two together; only B18b tests the mirror direction (unmark first, mark second). A regression that flips either half of that contract (e.g. a new query path that forgets the desc ordering, or a putIfAbsent that becomes an overwrite) would silently make an old bulk-mark override a later intentional unmark, and nothing in this suite would catch the positive-first/unmark-second direction.
recommendation: Add the described second _fakeLedgerData(..., entryScope: 'unmark_seder') entry after the positive one in B18 and assert the leaf remains learned (mirroring B18b's assertion in the opposite order); add a doc comment on computeLearnedLeafRefs stating the newest-first ordering precondition it relies on from callers.
acceptance_criteria: B18's ledgerEntries list contains both a positive seder entry and a corresponding unmark_seder entry, and the test fails if putIfAbsent semantics regress
computeLearnedLeafRefs doc comment states its ledgerEntries-must-be-newest-first-by-completedAt precondition
